---
title: "Getting Started"
---

`bgms` implements Bayesian estimation and edge selection for graphical models of mixed binary, ordinal, and continuous variables. Networks are estimated at the level of conditional associations: an edge between two variables indicates a direct relationship that persists after accounting for all other variables in the model.

The package has two main entry points:

- [`bgm()`](../reference/bgm.qmd) — fits a single network for one group of observations.
- [`bgmCompare()`](../reference/bgmCompare.qmd) — estimates and compares networks across independent groups.

For background on graphical models and the Bayesian approach, see [Graphical Models](graphical-models.qmd) and [The Bayesian Approach](bayesian-approach.qmd).

## Installation

### From CRAN

```r
install.packages("bgms")
```

### Development version

```r
if(!requireNamespace("remotes")) {
  install.packages("remotes")
}
remotes::install_github("Bayesian-Graphical-Modelling-Lab/bgms")
```

## Fitting a model

The main function is [`bgm()`](../reference/bgm.qmd). It accepts a data frame or matrix of mixed binary, ordinal, and continuous variables and estimates a Markov random field.

The Wenchuan dataset is included in the package, and contains ordinal measures of symptoms of posttraumatic stress from 362 survivors of the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake. 


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(bgms)

data(Wenchuan)
head(Wenchuan)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

[2,]         2      2     2     3       3       3        3       2       3
```

:::
:::



For illustration, we select five symptoms from the Wenchuan dataset — intrusive memories, disturbing dreams, flashbacks, emotional upset, and physical reactions — so that the output fits on screen:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
fit = bgm(Wenchuan[, 1:5], seed = 1234)
```
:::




By default, [`bgm()`](../reference/bgm.qmd) runs four parallel MCMC chains using the [No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS)](mcmc-diagnostics.qmd#nuts-specific-diagnostics) — the default sampling algorithm — in combination with Bayesian [edge selection](edge-selection.qmd). Here we use `seed = 1234` for reproducibility. If the sampler diagnostics indicate persistent problems, refit with `update_method = "adaptive-metropolis"`.

The summary shows posterior means, standard deviations, [Monte Carlo standard errors (MCSE)](mcmc-diagnostics.qmd#sec-mcse), [effective sample sizes (ESS)](mcmc-diagnostics.qmd#sec-ess), and [R-hat](mcmc-diagnostics.qmd#sec-rhat) values for each parameter. For partial associations, it also reports posterior inclusion probabilities because we used edge selection. For a full description of the output structure, see [MCMC Output](mcmc-output.qmd); for guidance on interpreting the convergence diagnostics (ESS and R-hat), see [MCMC Diagnostics](mcmc-diagnostics.qmd).

`coef()` returns posterior mean matrices: `$pairwise` contains the partial associations and `$indicator` contains edge inclusion probabilities.

## Network plot

To visualize the estimated network, we select the edges with posterior inclusion probabilities 0.5 or up, and plot the result using the `qgraph` package [@EpskampEtAl_2012_qgraph].


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(qgraph)

median_probability_network = coef(fit)$pairwise
median_probability_network[coef(fit)$indicator < 0.5] = 0.0

qgraph(median_probability_network,
  theme = "TeamFortress",
  maximum = 1,
  fade = FALSE,
  color = c("#f0ae0e"), vsize = 10, repulsion = .9,
  label.cex = 1, label.scale = "FALSE",
  labels = colnames(Wenchuan)[1:5]
)
```
:::



::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](getting-started_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){width=504}
:::
:::


In this plot, edges with posterior inclusion probability below 0.5 are set to zero. Practically, this means that a shown edge indicates evidence for a direct conditional association between two symptoms after accounting for the others in the network, whereas a missing edge indicates evidence that this direct association is absent at the selected threshold. Because the cutoff is 0.5, this reflects minimum evidence for inclusion (i.e., an inclusion Bayes factor threshold of 1 when prior inclusion probability is 0.5); higher posterior inclusion probabilities indicate stronger evidence for inclusion.

## Continuous data

For continuous variables, `bgms` fits a Gaussian graphical model. The interface is identical; only the `variable_type` argument changes. (All-continuous data also admit a dedicated Gibbs sampler via `update_method = "gibbs"`, which draws from exact conditionals with nothing to tune — see [Gaussian Graphical Model](ggm.qmd).)

## Next steps

- Learn about the unified [graphical model framework](graphical-models.qmd) in `bgms`, with [ordinal](omrf.qmd) and [continuous](ggm.qmd) special cases
- Understand [edge selection](edge-selection.qmd) with spike-and-slab priors
- Handle [missing data](missing-data.qmd) via listwise deletion or MCMC imputation
- Compare groups with [`bgmCompare()`](group-comparison.qmd)
- Discover edge communities with [Bayesian edge clustering](clustering.qmd)
